text.p: Swiss shares ended one percent higher in a recovery from Thursday's marked losses, but dealers said the correction may not yet be over.

"The rebound we saw today has not been very convincing," one trader noted, adding that volume remained rather low. But the firming tendency in the U.S. dollar and in bond futures was seen underpinning the market.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index close 48.2 points, or 1.08 percent, higher at 4,491.1 and the broad Swiss Performance Index advanced 25.90 points, or 0.92 percent, to end at 2,854.56.
The expiry of options and futures on Soffex was quiet, one dealer noted. But he said effects of the expiry may spill over into trading on Monday, leading to some volatility.
Pharmaceutical Roche, insurer Winterthur and financial concern Credit Suisse were among the more prominent winners.

Roche powered ahead 435 francs to 12,335 ahead of the 1996 results, due to be released on Monday after bourse close. There was also some speculation in the market that Roche may consider a buyback of participation certificates, as a CSFB study suggested.
CS Group added 3.75 francs to finish at 165. Winterthur ended 14 francs higher at 990 and Novartis registered shares closed five francs higher at 1,703.
UBS bearers gave up one franc to finish at 1,253. Alusuisse, Swiss Re, SMH all posted gains while Nestle recovered from stop loss orders to end with a 13 franc gain.
